solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unpleasant ending as late-night sit-in breaks up

indicators.note: a sit-in that breaks up is dispersed, so its letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Protesters staging an all-night occupation finally disperse, a sour end to the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks up' signals rearranging all fourteen letters of LATENIGHTSITIN; 'as' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a nasty surprise saved for the conclusion, like a scorpion's barb at the back.

clue.text: Secondary flower

definitions.meaning: crossword sense: something that flows, i.e. a river or stream

explanation.surface: A two-word description of some lesser bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but 'one that flows': a stream feeding a larger river.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream joining a bigger river is a subsidiary branch, and also something that flows; both readings fit.

clue.text: Assassin in Japan seen here

indicators.note: says the word can be seen right here within the clue's own letters, running across its words

explanation.surface: A caption pointing at a Japanese killer in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'assassiN IN JApan', and the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal Japan's covert agents were trained as spies and killers, the classic Japanese assassin.

clue.text: In France he joins a party that's narrow-minded

parts.note: the French word for 'he' is il
the Liberals were a British political party

explanation.surface: A Frenchman joins a political party described as intolerant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Party was a major British party, now merged into the Liberal Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intolerant of other views is unliberal in outlook, the plain dictionary sense.

clue.text: Time to reject starchy pudding when only these will fit!

indicators.note: rejecting something turns it back, so the pudding's word is written backwards

parts.note: sago is a starchy pudding made from palm pith

explanation.surface: After stuffing yourself with sago pudding, only loose garments will fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on overeating: after too much pudding, only loose Roman wraps would fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman robes were loose draped wraps of cloth, the sort of garment that fits any expanded waistline.

clue.text: Polish can be complicated

definitions.meaning: to refine or work out in more detail, a verb

explanation.surface: A remark that polishing work can be fiddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is a verb here, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means refine by adding detail; as an adjective it means intricate and detailed.

clue.text: Grant daughter gets in a top university

indicators.note: the daughter's letter gets in among the letters of the university phrase

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A girl wins a place at an elite college on a scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' is a verb, as in conceding a point, not a scholarship.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point in argument is to concede or acknowledge it as true.

clue.text: Generosity shown by Spanish leader to the audience

indicators.note: what an audience receives is what it hears, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: the first letter of Spanish is a capital, i.e. a large S

explanation.surface: A Spanish head of state displays generosity to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish leader' is not a king but its leading letter, a big S; saying 'large S' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means liberal giving of gifts or money, open-handed bounty.

clue.text: The revolutionary fled the capital

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so these three letters are rearranged

parts.note: ran away, ran

explanation.surface: A rebel escaped from the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' shuffles THE to TEH; the city is Iran's capital, fitting the revolution theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Bring back simple springwater

indicators.note: bringing a word back writes it in reverse order

parts.note: artless, naive

explanation.surface: A request to return to plain spring water.
explanation.definitionFit: Evian is a well-known French brand of bottled mineral water from a spring.

clue.text: Kind of hose that's a foot short

definitions.text: Kind of hose that's a foot short

parts.words: Kind of hose that's a foot short
parts.note: hose means stockings; this knitted tube covers the calf but stops before the foot

explanation.surface: A garden hose twelve inches too short to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' suggests a garden pipe and 'a foot' a measurement; really it is footless hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: This footless knitted tube for the calf, popular with dancers, is hosiery lacking the foot part.

clue.text: Possibly sweet mutterings in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a pudding course, as the stalks are stewed for dessert
the word extras repeat on stage to sound like crowd chatter

explanation.surface: Pleasant murmurs from a theatre audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' is the British word for dessert; stewed stalks of this plant are a classic one.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant's stalks make puddings, and actors murmur the word to simulate background crowd noise.

clue.text: Dog that is seen tracking lost explorer

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so this abbreviation comes after the explorer

parts.note: Captain Scott died returning from the South Pole
i.e., id est, that is

explanation.surface: A tracker dog searching for a missing explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal name for the Scottish terrier breed.

clue.text: Listener, welcomed by Poles, gets closer

indicators.note: being welcomed means taken in, so the listener goes inside the poles

parts.note: N and S, the north and south poles
an ear is what listens

explanation.surface: An eavesdropper welcomed by Polish people draws nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not Polish people but the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach is to come or draw closer to something.

clue.text: Sprout feathers to make a killing

parts.note: a shoot is a sprout of a plant
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Growing a crop of feathers to make a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a killing' sounds like profiting, but here it is literal: bringing down an aircraft or bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring down a plane or bird with gunfire is a literal killing rather than a profit.

clue.text: Takes part in foreplay?

parts.note: read as fore-play: performing a role ahead of the actual play, i.e. practising

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about sexual activity.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'foreplay' as before the play; taking a part in practice sessions ahead of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors practise their lines and moves before the performance, in the run-up to opening night.

clue.text: Frankfurter, only half-German, who shows off in 23, say

parts.note: a frankfurter sausage in a bun

indicators.note: only half of the word German is used, its front portion

explanation.surface: A frankfurter sausage that is only half German.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is CALIF, short for California; the definition is a show-off surfer or skier, typically Californian.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for someone performing flashy stunts, especially in surfing or skiing.

clue.text: Loss suffered by Humpty Dumpty

definitions.meaning: a deficit, an amount by which something falls below what is needed
the nursery-rhyme egg had a fall, and from a wall it is a fall that is not far

explanation.surface: A misfortune that befell the nursery-rhyme egg.
explanation.walkthrough: Humpty Dumpty is the egg in an English nursery rhyme who fell off a wall; read the answer as a brief tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit or gap between need and supply; read in two words it is a little tumble.

clue.text: You'd spend more than a penny here nowadays!

definitions.text: You'd spend more than a penny here nowadays!

parts.words: You'd spend more than a penny here nowadays!
parts.note: 'spend a penny' is British slang for using a lavatory, which once cost a penny coin

explanation.surface: A grumble about inflation: things cost more than a penny these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend a penny' is a British euphemism for urinating, from coin-operated public lavatories that cost one old penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated public lavatory, which now costs far more than the old penny.

clue.text: Competent (though sub-standard!) scripture lesson

indicators.note: sub means under, so in this down answer the word for competent sits below the standard

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
able, capable

explanation.surface: A capable but below-standard Bible lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub-standard' reads as poor quality but splits into 'sub' (beneath) and 'standard' (PAR).
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus taught through short moral stories in the Gospels, so such a story is a lesson from scripture.

clue.text: Tree starts to exfoliate, being old not young

indicators.note: the starts of the following five words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A tree shedding its bark, a sign of age rather than youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical hardwood tree yielding very dark, dense timber.

clue.text: Chicken-hearted or egg-hearted perhaps

definitions.meaning: an egg's heart, its yolk, is typically this colour

explanation.surface: Comparing a coward to a chicken or an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads 'hearted' literally: the centre of an egg has this colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word is slang for cowardly, and describes an egg yolk's hue.

clue.text: Strange creed requires it to be read allowed

indicators.note: something strange is altered from normal, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd creed that may only be read aloud with permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allowed' puns on 'aloud': the answer means spoken aloud from memory or text. 'Strange' rearranges CREED plus IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver words orally to an audience is to speak them out, as the pun on permitted suggests.

clue.text: Western state briefly with eastern ruler

indicators.note: briefly means in shortened form, so the state's name is cut down

parts.note: California, a state on the US west coast

explanation.surface: A US western state paired with an oriental monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims CALIFORNIA to its common abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of caliph, the title of a Muslim civil and religious leader.

clue.text: Democrat split leads to state of indecision

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
a rift is a split or rupture

explanation.surface: A division within the Democrats leaves the party dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless lack of direction or purpose, as in letting things wander along.

clue.text: Test includes section like the M25

indicators.note: one word includes another, so the section goes inside the test

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
a bit is a piece or section

explanation.surface: An exam with a question about a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway ringing London, known as the London Orbital.
explanation.definitionFit: A road circling a city is described as a ring road, going round like a satellite's path.

clue.text: Hot spicy dish from the sea, not cold

indicators.note: not cold means without the cold letter, so it is dropped

parts.note: the Baltic Sea in northern Europe
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A hot curry made from seafood, not served cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the sea' looks like seafood but 'the sea' is a named sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A curry cooked and served in a wok-like metal bowl, popular in Britain.

clue.text: Account unpaid being affected by inflation

parts.note: a bill is an account to be paid
owing, still due

explanation.surface: An unpaid bill growing because of rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' suggests economics, but the definition means literally swelling with air.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails or smoke swell outwards as they fill with air, a literal inflating.

clue.text: In S. America, plain students meet with a refusal!

parts.note: L is a learner, so LL is two students
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: South American students being plainly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner driver's plate in Britain; two of them make students.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a grassy plain, used for the vast grasslands of Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: A growing problem for Maman et Papa?

definitions.text: A growing problem for Maman et Papa?

parts.words: A growing problem for Maman et Papa?
parts.note: a French couple's troublesome child is literally a problem that is growing up

explanation.surface: French parents facing a problem that keeps getting bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing' means a child getting bigger; the French parents point to a French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: French for a terrible child, used of a shocking, unconventional person in their field.
